items.verified_scope: Nonreversible potential theory is an established baseline. The original assumes an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a countable space with stationary measure mu; its adjoint and energy use L2(mu). The inf-sup statement requires B complement finite. A sector constant is an additional hypothesis for an upper capacity comparison.
items.comparison_to_F271: The lattice-correction finite lemma instead begins with a finite doubly substochastic discrete-time U, killed coordinates and possible inaccessible closed classes. Its forward/adjoint residual and bounded-test energy estimate is a distinct specified interface. Do not import irreducibility, a stationary measure, certain absorption or the sector comparison without checking them. Classical direct finite harmonic linear algebra remains an old-method baseline; no new algorithmic gain has been tested.

The critical inverse temperature in this model is 3/[2 S(S+1)]. The interchange identification holds at spin 1/2 and is not general-spin equality.

items.verified_scope: Determinant preservation means expectation commutes with every square minor, not only the whole determinant. Scalar multiples of a fixed rank-one matrix are determinant preserving. Independent determinant-preserving matrices are closed under sums and products; the selected proof uses adjugate minors, fixed rank-one updates, conditioning and Cauchy-Binet.
items.comparison_to_F271: An independent Bernoulli transposition has the form I+s(T-I) with rank-one T-I, so the old rank-one and closure mechanism explains the admissible unconditioned exterior moments. This does not establish that conditioning on all cycles hitting pins preserves the property. The unnormalized next-pin identity plus its positive-probability Schur complement remains the specific F271 bridge to a conditional hitting first moment. No equality of full paths or arbitrary dependent products follows.
items.remaining: Applications to surrogate regression, MSE formulas, all empirical claims and Lemmas 5-6 proofs are not qualified here.
